pistons.headline: The Pistons go from owning to getting owned in the paint
pistons.body:
DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 04: Jalen Duren #0 of the Detroit Pistons looks on from the bench during a game against the Philadelphia 76ers at Little Caesars Arena on November 04, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images

During a tumultuous playoff run and a prolonged offseason contract negotiation, Detroit Pistons fans were ready to say goodbye to Jalen Duren. Well, Duren has been out for six of eight games, and it turns out that Duren is the most indispensable member of the Pistons aside from Cade Cunningham.

A hamstring strain has knocked Duren out for six straight and counting, and boy, do you feel that every moment of every Pistons game.

Pundits and fans alike had easy diagnoses for what ailed the 60-win team during a disappointing second-round exit last season. Detroit needed a second scorer and much more perimeter shooting to succeed in the postseason. Its second-best player, the All-NBA big man Duren, couldn’t effectively operate in a congested, constipated offense when opponents had so much extra time to prepare their defense. That had a trickle-down effect on Cade Cunningham and on offensively limited players the Pistons relied on, like Ausar Thompson, Javonte Green, and Ron Holland.

This offseason, the Pistons seemingly tried and failed to add their second scorer (a planned run at Austin Reaves fizzled, and trade interest in players such as Kyrie Irving and Kevin Durant went nowhere). But they certainly addressed the team’s lack of perimeter punch. Detroit added guys such as Isaiah Joe, John Collins, and Taurean Prince. They re-signed midseason acquisition Kevin Huerter. They reformulated their offensive game plan to create more movement, space, and offensive responsibility among their non-Cade players. So far this season, the perimeter offense has hummed. Detroit is a top-10 team in 3-point shooting and almost middle of the pack in attempts despite Isaiah Joe missing most of the season to injury.

Detroit is 6-2, losing to the New York Knicks and on Wednesday night to the East-leading Philadelphia 76ers. Calls after both games from fans and casual watchers immediately turn to the team’s lack of that second star as the biggest issue. While that still might be a deal-breaker in the players, I would argue that the actual biggest issue in the season’s first eight games is Detroit’s collapse in its former ability to absolutely own the paint.

In other words, it’s not the lack of a Kyrie or a Durant or a Devin Booker. It’s the lack of Duren.

Last season, Detroit led the NBA in points in the paint, mostly behind Duren’s elite rim gravity and chemistry with Cade Cunningham and Detroit’s other ball handlers. Last season, the Pistons led the NBA with 57.9 points in the paint and were fourth in opponents’ paint scoring. They had a scoring differential inside of 14.2 points per game.  This season, Detroit ranks just 22nd in the paint at 44.8, down 13.1 points per game.

Rim gravity, it turns out, is just as important as perimeter shooting in creating the space needed to run a successful offense.

Paul Reed is a dynamic scorer inside, and he has some pop to his game. But he isn’t a rim runner like Duren. You give it to him on the block, and you let him work his magic. John Collins is opportunistic in transition, but those opportunities are dried up when he is the only big on the floor applying rim pressure, usually trying to duck in from the corners.

Ausar has the ball in his hands more, and it is working to create opportunities from others on the perimeter, but it is taking away a lot of those dunker-spot opportunities and back cuts that Thompson feasted on last season.

The lack of inside pressure is manifesting in other ways. Detroit has gone from a top-5 team in second-chance points to 22nd. They are 28th in offensive rebounding. Last season, they were third.

This team needs Jalen Duren back ASAP. And I think fans need to start reckoning with how crucial he is for this team to succeed.

pistons.headline: Pistons vs 76ers final score: Detroit falls short in East battle
pistons.body:
DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 04: Cade Cunningham #2 of the Detroit Pistons drives around Vj Edgecombe #77 of the Philadelphia 76ers during the first half at Little Caesars Arena on November 04, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images

The Detroit Pistons (6-2) fall short in the battle between the top teams in the Eastern Conference. The Philadelphia 76ers (8-1) outlasted Detroit 112-106. Philly got up by as many as 18 points, but Detroit never truly went away. The 76ers’ stardom showed its head tonight.

After holding Jaylen Brown to 16 points in the first meeting of the season, he surpassed that in the first half this time around. Brown poured in 30 points for the game while converting on 11 of his 19 shots. He rained in spot-up 3s, as it was tough to stick with him with the way Philly forced Detroit into scramble mode throughout the ballgame. Brown had a clutch block on Cade, and his presence was felt on both sides of the ball.

This is not 2023 Joel Embiid, but he’s still a force. Embiid still draws double teams and can get any big in foul trouble. He and Tolu Smith got into a dust-up that injected some life into Detroit, but Philly found a way to withstand every Detroit storm.

Duncan Robinson went on a few personal runs that seemed to turn the tide in Detroit’s favor. The sharpshooter went for 27 points and buried an unconscious seven triples. Robinson’s ability to look past the hands in his face to shoot the rock will pay dividends all season. It didn’t work out tonight, but Robinson is off to a different type of start as a sniper.

Cade Cunningham tried to put on his cape and emptied the clip. He couldn’t find it from deep but got good looks. He went for 26 points, 11 assists, and seven boards. He got to the charity stripe and nailed every attempt (7-7). Cade had another LeBron-like chasedown block — this time in LeBron’s presence.

At this point, those are truly Cade-like chasedowns, and Brown’s missed layup here shows Cade’s reputation as a chasedown artist is evident.

Jaylen Brown misses the wide open layup. 😬 pic.twitter.com/jMyfS41RJG
— Hoop Central (@TheHoopCentral) November 5, 2026

VJ Edgecombe had a fast break sequence where he u-turned it because Cade was on the hunt again. Special defender.

Ausar Thompson’s special stuff came on the boards as he snagged 17 rebounds tonight. From the opening possession, he was pogo-sticking down low to help Paul Reed and John Collins in the paint. AT chipped in 11 points, and his shot from the line continues to look better. He was 3-for-4 tonight; you’ll take the small improvements wherever you can.

John Collins had his best offensive game in a few games. He was getting behind the defense, throwing down head-top slams. His ability to be a paint finisher and hit threes is why he’s here. He only shot one 3 tonight. The Pistons need more.

Collins should look better when Duren comes back, in theory. Duren has rim-gravity that forces defenses to account for one of the best finishers in basketball. This was the first game where I thought Detroit missed Duren badly. From a talent perspective, Detroit was outgunned tonight.

LeBron James controlled the tempo in spurts of the game. He was playing like that OG at the Y who’s keeping up with the youngins on pure know-how. LeBron draws two to the ball, Embiid does, Brown does, and Tyrese Maxey does. There’s a lot of star power over there, and this is a team Detroit could see in the long run.

The Pistons did not have their sharpest defensive night, and Philly still only cracked 112. It was just one of the games. Detroit shifts their focus to another superstar in Luka Dončić. He and the Los Angeles Lakers travel to Detroit on Sunday as the Pistons take on their first Western Conference team of the season.

The Detroit Pistons are looking to keep the good times rolling against the Philadelphia 76ers. Detroit and Philly are the two best teams in the East, and the Pistons have already notched one win against the Sixers this season. In fact, the 106-93 win in October was Detroit’s sixth consecutive victory against Philly. Tonight, they go for lucky No. 7. That loss against the Pistons also happens to be Philadelphia’s lone blemish on the season. In that matchup, the Pistons were without the services of Jalen Duren. It worked out because they were able to rely on the all-around goodness of Paul Reed. It also didn’t hurt that Joel Embiid missed that first matchup to rest.

Tonight, the Pistons will have no such luck. They are still missing All-Star big man Duren, and tonight the Sixers will employ the services of their former MVP in Embiid. While Detroit has been playing amazing basketball, they have been vulnerable down low, and Embiid will be the best interior big man they’ve faced since they lost Duren to a hamstring injury.

One benefit in Detroit’s favor is that this is a nationally televised game on ESPN, and it seems like Cade Cunningham loves to come up big when the lights are brightest for national television. Cunningham is also coming off of perhaps his most dominant performance of the season, scoring 33 points in just 26 minutes of action. If the game against the Hornets was close instead of a 30-point blowout late, if seems like Cunningham could have gone for 45 points.

pistons.headline: Pistons vs 76ers preview:  East’s top two teams square off on National TV
pistons.body:
If you are to believe preseason predictions, this game being a showdown between the East’s top two teams could come as a bit of a surprise.  Pistons fans knew this team would be good, but many talking heads predicted a falloff this season while everybody was on board with the 76ers being one of the best teams in the league.

It shouldn’t come as a surprise that the team that was 1st in the East last season is once again competing for the top seed in the East, but talking heads have to make their money somehow.  ESPN at least had the foresight to pickup this game and you get what should be a very fun early-season showdown between two teams that have only lost one game each.

The 76ers and Pistons have played once this season and the Pistons won, but it is tough to draw any conclusions since both teams were missing a couple of starters.

Game Vitals

Where:  Little Caesars Arena in Detroit, MI
When:  Wednesday, November 4 at 7 pm EST
Watch:  ESPN
Odds:  Detroit (-2.5)

Analysis

The Pistons will be without Jalen Duren and Isaiah Joe, who was already ruled out for this game last night.  The Pistons were missing Jalen Duren in the last matchup between these teams and also Ausar Thompson, who they will have back.  But, Isaiah Joe did suffer the hip injury that is still keeping him out during the 1st quarter of the last matchup, so the Pistons are trading one injured player for another.

With this being a National TV game and the 76ers getting a day of rest, I would suspect that everybody plays for them tonight.  In the last matchup, the 76ers did not have Joel Embiid or VJ Edgecombe, which really put their lack of depth to the test.

Joel Embiid’s size and ability on the glass could become a problem for the Pistons, who will continue to start the undersized Paul Reed and likely use John Collins to back him up.  Without Jalen Duren, rebounding was already going to be a problem, but the Pistons have been able to overcome it during his absence.

In the last matchup, the Pistons were able to contain Tyrese Maxey through 3 quarters before he started hitting shots in the 4th.  It was a bit of shocking development since the Pistons were without Ausar Thompson, but without some of the other stars for the 76ers, they could focus their defense more on stopping Maxey.  The 76ers have a lot of star power, but their biggest offensive threat is arguably Maxey, who can hit shots from anywhere on the court and can use his quickness with the ball to get to where he wants.  I would expect Ausar Thompson to draw the Tyrese Maxey matchup which will allow Cade Cunningham to guard Jaylen Brown since he has the size to keep up with him.

I am not really sure what the Pistons are going to do about the Joel Embiid matchup.  Paul Reed is outsized by him and also can have some issues with fouling and Joel Embiid has made a living off of bating fouls throughout his career.  Paul Reed is going to have to stay disciplined, as I don’t think the Pistons can afford to have heavy minutes of John Collins at center or Tolu Smith.  I have full confidence in the Pistons’ ability to matchup with the rest of the 76ers starting lineup, but the most concern I have is this matchup and it very well could swing the game.

If there is one certainty for the Pistons, it is that Cade Cunningham is difficult to slow down, especially with how he is playing now.  He is coming off a 33 points masterclass against the Charlotte Hornets on Monday in only 27 minutes where he absolutely took over the game and turned a single-digit lead into a 20-plus point blowout.  Cade Cunningham always starts off the season slow, but he seems to be hitting his stride now.  His 3-ball is consistently falling as he is shooting 37% from beyond the arc, which is a significant development for his offensive creation abilities and efficiency.

He is going to have to put together another masterclass if the Pistons want any hope to win this game.  During Jalen Duren’s absence, the Pistons have been able to win games through their high-level defense, but their offense has left a lot to be desired.  With Isaiah Joe out and Duncan Robinson going through a bit of a cold stretch, the Pistons shooting fell off a bit and they went four games in a row scoring 110 points or less.

However, everything seemed to get back on track on Monday against the Hornets, so hopefully that continues.

One player the Pistons are hoping gets back on track is John Collins.  He had his best game as a Piston in the last game against the 76ers and has proceeded to score single-digit points in every game since then.  With Jalen Duren out, he has had to play a lot more center than he was probably planning on playing, but he has also had difficulties finding a consistent offensive role.  Another big John Collins game would be a huge help in this matchup

The Joel Embiid matchup concerns me with the Pistons lack of frontcourt size, but if they can defend Tyrese Maxey like they did in the last matchup, they have a shot to takedown the 76ers and claim the top seed in the Eastern Conference.

Lineups

Detroit Pistons (6-1):  Cade Cunningham, Duncan Robinson, Ausar Thompson, John Collins, Paul Reed

Philadelphia 76ers (7-1):  Tyrese Maxey, VJ Edgecombe, Jaylen Brown, LeBron James, Joel Embiid

Question of the Day

Which of these teams will finish higher in the Eastern Conference at the end of the season?

pistons.headline: Pistons vs. Hornets final score: Cade Cunningham powers second-half surge in blowout win
pistons.body:
CHARLOTTE, NC - NOVEMBER 2: Cade Cunningham #2 of the Detroit Pistons looks on during the game against the Charlotte Hornets on November 2, 2026 at Spectrum Center in Charlotte, North Carolina. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Kent Smith/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images

The Detroit Pistons played great basketball throughout the night, but the Charlotte Hornets just kept hanging around. The Pistons were shooting better than 60% from the floor and 50% from three, and yet a Dennis Schroder layup made it a two-possession game with just under five minutes left in the second quarter. Then Cade Cunningham took over, then the Detroit Pistons took over, and suddenly a squeaker turned into a 124-91 Detroit win.

In that decisive 45-16 run, Cade Cunningham scored 14 points, and he did it in under three and a half minutes of game time. One of the league’s best players finally had his first superstar quarter of the season, scoring 17 points and notching three assists in total in that decisive third frame. He finished the night with 33 points, seven assists, and five steals. In those magical few minutes, he was everywhere in his bag. Patient mid-range pull-ups, slicing through the D for layups, catch-and-shoot threes. He went to the bench with 1:17 left in the third quarter, and you were left thinking he might hit 50 in the fourth. But he never needed to come back in the game again.

He saw the game was getting too close, and he decided to do something about it. He put the team on his back and said, “We’re playing too well to not blow these guys out.”

But the true blowout wouldn’t have happened without all the other contributions up and down the lineup. The Pistons really have something on offense this season, and while the range of ball handlers and actions can lead to some self-inflicted wounds, it is designed to open up this offense and let it breathe. And, boy, did they take a big gulping breath versus the Hornets.

The Pistons shot 57% from the floor and 48% from deep, and that was dragged down a bit as a consequence of some extended garbage time. The Pistons also kept their defense in top form. They forced 25 Charlotte turnovers, and that led to 27 fast-break points.

Detroit was led by Cade, but Duncan Robinson continues to be lights out this season. He shot 6-of-9 from deep on his way to 24 points. His stroke was immediate and effortless. He’s truly in the zone. Some of that shooting magic might be rubbing off on Kevin Huerter. The one-time bucket has struggled from deep for a few seasons now, including his short stint after a mid-season trade to Detroit last season. But he hit three threes tonight and is now shooting 38% from deep for the season. Even Ron Holland canned three threes tonight. Not to be overlooked is Ausar Thompson’s expanded role in the offense.

It’s not always perfect, but Thompson is getting more comfortable making decisions with the ball in his hands, and he’s understanding how to make defense pay by using his strength and burst to get something close to the basket. Thompson was 5-of-7 from the floor for 14 points, and he added six rebounds and four assists.

The Pistons had plenty of lopsided runs last season in their sprint to 60 wins. But those were driven by a defense that would suffocate you and an offense that could do just enough. Last year, the Pistons could go on a 27-2 run over the course of 17 minutes of game action. Tonight, they went on the same run in just over eight minutes.

Detroit’s defense remains the best in the league. Its offense is starting to catch up. That’s bad news for everyone else in the NBA.

It’s already time for a rematch, huh? The Detroit Pistons face the Charlotte Hornets for the second time this season. In the first matchup, the Pistons prevailed 97-89 behind a Cade Cunningham and Daniss Jenkins one-two punch at point guard. Cunningham had 30 points and seven assists, and Jenkins scored 14 points off the bench. They also got great contributions from Paul Reed (16 efficient points) and an all-around masterclass from Ausar Thompson, who tallied seven points, nine rebounds, and eight assists. It featured a great 31-point performance from the blossoming Brandon Miller and one of the season’s earliest head-scratchers. Naz Reid had seven points and six rebounds at halftime, but Hornets coach Charles Lee benched Reid for the entire second half for not meeting the “standards” of the team. Nothing stood out as egregious, and folks chalked it up to mixing up some defensive assignments and a lack of hustle. It was a surprising but short-lived kerfuffle (Reid’s been back in the lineup ever since). But I wouldn’t be surprised if the Hornets power forward is looking to make a statement against Detroit so as to truly put the situation to rest.

The Hornets are struggling to find their offense after moving on from LaMelo Ball and getting a bum hand via injuries — Kon Knueppel and Grant Williams are both going to miss the game tonight. That means the league’s least potent (statistically) offense is going to go up against the league’s most miserly defense (statistically). pistons.headline: Pistons vs Nets final score: Detroit takes care of business in first NBA Cup game
pistons.body:
BROOKLYN, NY - OCTOBER 30: Ronald Holland II #5 of the Detroit Pistons dunks the ball during the game against the Brooklyn Nets during the 2026 Emirates NBA Cup on October 30, 2026 at Barclays Center in Brooklyn, New York. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Nathaniel S. Butler/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images

The Detroit Pistons start the NBA Cup off with a bang. Detroit thumped the Brooklyn Nets 110-94. A plus-16 point differential is a solid start on their quest to win their first NBA Cup in franchise history.

Detroit’s defense got off to an uncharacteristic start. They got mixed up on several pick-and-roll possessions, but that didn’t last long. They figured out the Nets’ speedy guards. Nolan Traoré turns on the turbos when turning the corners. Detroit adjusted to his speed and Julius Randle’s bully ball style of play.

For the second straight game, Detroit held their opponents to a seemingly never-ending scoring drought. The Pistons hard-hedged, blitzed, and switched PnRs depending on their personnel on the floor. It’s a luxury to have so many versatile defenders.

The John Collins at the five lineups always present a different look. It’s a lot of speed out there when Detroit goes small. The lineups with Paul Reed aren’t technically small ball, but J.B. Bickerstaff can employ him so many different ways. Reed is not too much of a drop big, but he pressures guards coming off screens in every other way.

When Detroit did go small, Duncan Robinson and Kevin Huerter got their hands dirty helping the team gang rebound. It didn’t register in the box score every time, but the fight was there. Huerter was scrappy and hit a pair of first-half triples. His explosion from trey is coming. I will remain patient and will take all the other little things he’s doing.

Robinson is off to a career-best start. The 3s were hit or miss, but he thrived in transition and baited Brooklyn into several turnovers. Robinson is such an educated cutter. Teams press up on him, sticking to him like gum under the desk, but he has no issue using their momentum against them, beelining to the rim.

Robinson and Ausar connected on some backdoor cuts. Their synergy is so evident. They burned another defense with their DHO link-up.

We got aggressive Ausar tonight. Right from the opening tap, he searched for his shot and was content to put his head down to get to the rim.

Ausar Thompson that was beautiful pic.twitter.com/1Z3C6BE6Nd
— mm (@muhtxm) October 31, 2026

We got a middy pull-up in the second! Ausar was feeling it and took another jumper the following possession. Make or miss, that is the mentality that can change this team’s outlook.

Ausar’s all-around play was terrific. We’re watching a legit point forward in the making game by game. Ausar had six assists tonight. This one was gorgeous.

Ausar with the behind the back dish 👀 pic.twitter.com/rhArT0m6sk
— Detroit Pistons (@DetroitPistons) October 31, 2026

Ausar’s 9-to-5 defensive intensity clone, Ron Holland, had himself a ball game. He had a turnover and ill-advised fouls early on, but Holland turned it up a notch in the 3rd quarter.

The third-year wing was EVERYWHERE. His hound-em defense showed up, but Holland buried two 3-pointers during his energy blitz. He finished with 18 points, going 6-for-10 from the field, along with four steals.

It was another day in the office for Deuce. He might be the first player to get a foul called in their favor in real time. He did the classic Kobe/DWade up fake, then shoot while the defender is off their feet. It did not seem like the referee was going to reward Cade’s craftiness until he walked over there with wide-spread arms demanding an explanation. Nice to see Cade getting that superstar whistle these days. He dropped 20/5/4.

Brooklyn remains winless (0-5). Traoré is a blur, and Mikel Brown Jr. seems to process PnR coverages like a point guard who’s been around the block. That dude has promise. High process and deep-range shooting is always a dub in my book. Brooklyn fans won’t enjoy watching Randle go one-on-one with 10 eyes staring at him, waiting for his drive, but hey, it’s not all bad elsewhere. Focus on the young guards.

Ebuka Okorie probably gets more run in a typical blowout. Detroit aimed to run up the score for the cup point differential, so that might explain why Bickerstaff went with his proven horses until it was less than three minutes in the contest.

Detroit’s 2025 second-round pick Chaz Lanier got in on the action. He knocked down two deep balls with his quick trigger release. This was a monster performance from Detroit after their defense got back on a string. Brooklyn isn’t the 1996 Bulls but has competed in most of their games so far. Not tonight.

Detroit looks to beat up on the Charlotte Hornets again to kick off their November schedule on Monday. Maybe they get Charlotte so discombobulated that Charles Lee has to bench another starter.

(Daniss had another end-of-quarter buzzer-beater. Add this one to the highlight reel)

He's good at that. https://t.co/sYGm01ubBO pic.twitter.com/b6SJHj4SCu
— Detroit Pistons (@DetroitPistons) October 31, 2026

pistons.headline: The Pindown: The Pistons are a Good Team… Again
pistons.body:
While Robbie is out celebrating, Blake returns to discuss the impressive wins the Pistons have earned over the past week. The Detroit Lions (5-2) and Miami Dolphins (1-6) will square off in Week 9, with the Lions looking to extend their three-game winning streak—and the Dolphins seeking their second win of the season.

“(Dolphins Head) Coach (Jeff) Hafley’s done a good job in his first year,” Lions coach Dan Campbell said on Wednesday. “A lot of similarities to—just reminds me a little of what we were when we came in. They’re young, they’re hungry, they’re active. They run, they hit, they hustle, they finish, try to play disciplined ball, and they’re playing that way.”

Let’s take a closer look at the Dolphins’ coaching staff, the scheme they run, and scouting notes from their most recently viewed games.

Dolphins head coach: Jeff Hafley

Head coaching seasons: 1st in the NFL
NFL coaching seasons: 10th season (Dolphins, Packers, 49ers, Browns, Bucs)
Defensive coordinator: 2 seasons (Packers 2024-25)
Other coaching roles held: DBs coach, Head Coach Boston College (2020-23), DC at Ohio State (2019)
Influences: Robert Saleh (scheme); Greg Schiano (Xs & Os), Dave Wannstedt (leadership)
Coached under: Kyle Shanahan, Saleh, Schiano, Wannstedt, Matt LaFleur, Mike Pettine, and Ryan Day (OSU)
Lions coaching connection: Jim O’Neil (Lions safeties coach/Assistant head coach) was the Browns DC in 2014-15 and the 49ers DC in 2016 when Hafley was the DBs coach for both teams
Play caller: Yes

Offensive coordinator: Bobby Slowik

NFL coaching seasons: 13th season (Dolphins, Texans, 49ers, Washington)
Offensive coordinator seasons: 4th season (Dolphins 2025-present, Texans 2023-24)
Previous coaching positions: Passing game coordinator, pass game specialist, offensive & defensive assistant
Influences: Mike and Kyle Shanahan, Mike McDaniel, Matt Lafleur, Sean McVay
Coached under: Shanahan, Shanahan, McDaniel, and DeMeco Ryans

Offensive scheme

Passing game: Shanahan Spread
Running scheme: Outside zone
Scouting notes:

Shanahan Core principles: marry pass and run, Shotgun looks (52%), lean on play-action (26.6%, 11th in the NFL), bunch formations, screens, etc.

11 personnel (58%) is the primary staple

21 personnel (28%) – traditional FB usage

12 personnel (9.3%)

Blocking scheme balance: Outside Zone (24%), Man (20%), Inside Zone (14%), Power (12.5%), Puller (7%), Counter (7%)

Prefer to get downhill with RB Ollie Gordon, with electric RB De’Von Achane on IR (ACL)

Rushing yards per game: 123.3 (11th); Rush yards per play: 4.4 (11th)

Heavy reliance on explosive plays over consistency in the run game

Explosives: EPA per rush: -0.03 (10th); Explosive run plays: 16.7% (3rd); 10+ yard rushes: 26 (7th)

Consistency is low: Success rate: 38.7% (20th); DVOA rushing: 26th; Stuffed Rate: 20% (26th)

Passing game is not clicking; DVOA passing: 26th

Passing yards per game: 166.7 (30th)

EPA per pass: -0.16 (24th); Explosive passing game: 24th

Pressures allowed (7 games): 99 (16th); Pressure rate: 43.2% (31st); Time to pressure: 2.77 (27th)

Sacks allowed: 21 (21st); Sack rate: 10.3% (31st)

RPO/rollout/bootleg concepts with QB Malik Willis to buy time in muddy pocket

Dan Campbell on Dolphins offense:

“Offensively, they really have an athletic offensive line that’s got mass. They run a versatile scheme. (RB Ollie) Gordon is a heavy back. You give him a lane, and he can hit it, hit it with speed, build the speed, and that’s where he gets dangerous. You let him hit the line of scrimmage with any type of speed and any crease and he can go. […] There’s a ton of this eye candy and motions and cutting the defense off. It’s a good scheme and they run it well, screens, gadgets, play pass off of it. (QB) Malik (Willis)’s done a heck of a job with all that stuff. (WR) Malik Washington, they got young receivers outside that are growing, up and coming, growing. Washington is a good football player, plays in the slot, he can play outside and he’s also their punt returner. So, he’s pretty dynamic in that regard. Look, this is a hungry team and they’re playing good football.”

Defensive coordinator: Sean Duggan

NFL coaching seasons: 3rd season (Dolphins, Packers)
Defensive coordinator seasons: 1st season

Influences: Jeff Hafley, Matt LaFleur
Coached under: Hafley, LaFleur

DETROIT, MICHIGAN - SEPTEMBER 14: Head coach Ben Johnson of the Chicago Bears and Head coach Dan Campbell of the Detroit Lions shake hands following the game at Ford Field on September 14, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images

The NFL trade deadline is coming soon (next Tuesday), and with such a tightly contested NFC North, there could be an arms race on the horizon. Currently the Minnesota Vikings lead the division at 6-1, but the 5-2 Detroit Lions and 6-2 Chicago Bears are close behind, and both teams are hunting to add more talent before Tuesday’s deadline. In fact, according to ESPN insider Dan Graziano, both the Lions and Bears could be hunting for the same players.

In one of his latest pieces for ESPN, Graziano said both the Lions and Bears have made calls about acquiring a cornerback.

“The Bears made their big move for [Jeffery] Simmons, but they’re still poking around on potentially available cornerbacks, as are the Lions,” Graziano wrote this week. “Detroit might also be in the market for help at linebacker, particularly in the wake of the terrible injury to mainstay Jack Campbell.”

It’s no surprise to hear that the Lions are still searching for a cornerback. The team admitted they were in the market for Joey Porter Jr. before he was eventually traded to the Dallas Cowboys. And the Lions’ cornerback situation hasn’t really changed since. While D.J. Reed is certainly playing better as the team’s No. 1 cornerback in recent weeks, Detroit is still seeking a No. 2 cornerback while rotating through the likes of Roger McCreary, Rock Ya-Sin, Khalil Dorsey, and Ennis Rakestraw.

The Bears, who already made a big trade deadline move by sending two first-round picks and more to the Titans for defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, have also dealt with some issues in the secondary. No. 1 cornerback Jaylon Johnson is currently ranked 103rd out of 106 qualifying cornerbacks in PFF coverage grade (32.1), while CB2 Malik Muhammad isn’t faring much better (52.5, 78th).

At this point, it isn’t clear which cornerbacks are available to acquire at the trade deadline. But some of the more commonly thrown around names are Eagles cornerback Riq Woolen, Commanders cornerback Mike Sainristil, Dolphins cornerback JuJu Brent, and Chargers cornerback Donte Jackson. A month ago, we also compiled a list of defensive backs that the Lions could target at the trade deadline.

We’ll see if either team can pull off a move with just days remaining before the deadline.

lions.headline: Discussion: Which Detroit Lions player needs to step up most in light of injuries?
lions.body:
Aug 3, 2026; Allen Park, MI, USA; Detroit Lions linebacker Malcolm Rodriguez (44) smiles as he talks with linebacker Derrick Barnes (55) following Detroit Lions training camp. Mandatory Credit: Paul Barnick-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect

The Detroit Lions’ Wednesday injury report was as long as it’s been all season. On top of Jimmy Rolder being placed on injured reserve earlier this week, the following Lions players were  estimated to not be able to practice:

C Cade Mays (ankle)

EDGE DJ Wonnum (concussion)

LB Jack Campbell (neck)

CB D.J. Reed (hip)

Additionally, these players were estimated to be limited in practice:

RB Jacob Saylors (neck)

WR Amon-Ra St. Brown (rib)

LB Amen Ogbongbemiga (toe)

S Kerby Joseph (knee)

S Brian Branch (concussion)

That’s six Lions defenders and nine total players with their status up in the air this week. It’s far too early to declare any of these players definitively out this week (outside of Kerby Joseph—Dan Campbell already said he won’t play this week—and Jack Campbell), but there’s a pretty good likelihood the Lions will be missing at least a couple of these players.

So today’s Question of the Day is:

Which Lions players need to step up the most vs. the Dolphins?

My answer: It feels like the answer has to come on defense. With Campbell and Rolder out, there will certainly be a ton of extra pressure on the linebacker room. Derrick Barnes, Malcolm Rodriguez, and Trevor Nowaske are the most likely starters for Detroit this week, and we’ve seen a lot of ups and downs from this group. The good news is that they all have plenty of experience on defense. The bad news is that none of them bring the consistent play-making ability of Campbell, nor the leadership of Detroit’s defensive captain.

But relief can also come from a different position. Covering the middle of the field has been a challenge, and it’s not necessarily a strength of the current linebacking corps. This would be a huge week for the safeties to step up. While it’s unclear if Branch will be available this week, I’m really looking for Chuck Clark and Keith Abney to elevate their games. Abney has been up and down, as you’d expect from a rookie who made a midseason shift from cornerback to safety. But I’ve been pretty disappointed with how Clark has played. He was supposed to bring communication and discipline to the position, but mental errors have plagued the back end (admittedly, not all his fault).

Malik Willis is not afraid to throw deep or utilize the middle of the field, so I’d love to see a clean game from the safeties to help out the ailing linebacker position.

Rolder injured his hamstring last Sunday, and with the injury potentially requiring surgery, he’s being shut down for the remainder of the season. While that ends his rookie season, the good news is he should be able to return in 2027.

Jack Campbell update

I wanted to take a moment to talk about Jack Campbell, as most Lions fans are anxiously awaiting updates on his status and wondering about his future, both on and off the field. First, in case you missed it, Jack Campbell released a statement earlier on Wednesday; here’s an excerpt (emphasis is the author’s):

“I’m incredibly encouraged by the progress I’ve made in such a short period of time. I have full movement in my lower body, and I’m continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body. I know there’s still work ahead, but I remain very optimistic. I’m taking things one day at a time, staying positive, and focusing on getting better.”

Jack is still on the 53-man roster and hasn’t been moved to injured reserve, but it would be improper to speculate why a move has or hasn’t been made at this time. The team typically takes their time in these situations, so it’s important to be patient right now and not make assumptions either way.

For now, the team is preparing to turn to Juice Scruggs against the Dolphins.

Wonnum is in the NFL’s concussion protocol and must pass a series of steps before he can move forward. Every player deals with head injuries differently, so we will have to wait and see how he is able to handle the increasing stressors deployed in the protocol.

Reed was forced out of the Vikings game late, and while he didn’t return, he was available in the locker room after the game, which is typically a good sign for his injury. The Lions will likely take it slow with their top corner this week.

lions.headline: Lions promote LB Joe Bachie to active roster, sign two other LBs
lions.body:
CINCINNATI, OH - AUGUST 13: Detroit Lions linebacker Joe Bachie (35) walks off the field at halftime during the preseason game between the Detroit Lions and the Cincinnati Bengals at Paycor Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Cincinnati, OH. (Photo by Ian Johnson/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images

The Detroit Lions announced three linebacker-related roster transactions on Wednesday: signing Joe Bachie from the practice squad to the active roster, signing K.J. Britt from the Patriots’ practice squad to the active roster, and signing Owen Pappoe to the practice squad.

No immediate roster moves were necessary, as the Lions previously opened two spots on their 53-man roster on Tuesday when they placed rookie linebacker Jimmy Rolder on injured reserve and waived rookie safety Bishop Fitzgerald. Bachie’s promotion from the practice squad opened a spot for Pappoe.

Bachie joined the Lions in April and provided veteran experience throughout training camp at MIKE linebacker and on special teams. He performed well enough in the preseason to be firmly on the roster bubble, and while the Lions released him in cutdowns, they signed him back to the practice squad the next day. When it became clear Rolder couldn’t start the season due to injury, the Lions signed Bachie to the active roster for their first two games, then released him in late September and re-signed him to the practice squad.

With Bachie operating as the team’s LB7, the injuries to Jack Campbell and Rolder have created a need for him to step into a larger role moving forward. While he will almost certainly be a fixture on special teams, his experience and positional versatility could put him at LB4 behind Derrick Barnes, Trevor Nowaske, and Malcolm Rodriguez, the three presumed starters.

As for Britt and Pappoe, it will likely take time for them to acclimate to the Lions’ defensive scheme. That said, Britt has plenty of special teams experience, and with the Lions’ preference to keep six linebackers active on game days, he could be active as soon as this Sunday against the Dolphins.

lions.headline: How Detroit Lions plan to channel Jack Campbell emotions into Dolphins prep
lions.body:
DETROIT,MICHIGAN-NOVEMBER 1: Head coach Dan Campbell of the Detroit Lions reacts during an NFL football game between the Minnesota Vikings and the Detroit Lions in Detroit, Michigan USA, on Sunday, November 1, 2026 (Photo by Amy Lemus/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images

The mental strain on this Detroit Lions team cannot be easy this week. Even with the great news that linebacker Jack Campbell has full movement in his lower body after a traumatic neck injury on Sunday, it’s natural for the entire locker room to have their attention divided between Campbell’s recovery and Sunday’s upcoming game against the Miami Dolphins.

Lions coach Dan Campbell isn’t running away from that difficult reality.

“There’s no easy way to do this, but you also have to acknowledge it, and let’s talk about it and make sure we know,” Campbell said. “But I also know they’re not postponing this game. And I know the only way to honor Jack, we know the only way to really honor Jack and what he really wants is to make sure that we’re locked in and ready to go because otherwise what just kind of came about, then we’re throwing it away in a sense.”

Like any other week, the Lions have mental health professionals in-house to help any players who may need support or just a person to talk to. Campbell indicated that there are players who have already utilized those resources this week.

Lions coach Scottie Montgomery is taking a similar approach to Dan Campbell, noting that it’s impossible to ignore their “fallen leader.”

“The key word is balance. The human in all of us—we play football, we coach football, but our first element is the human element,” Montgomery said. “It’s very difficult, of course, emotionally to be in a game like that, having a situation like that happen. And what we do have to talk about, we can’t ignore; we have had open dialogue. We do this with our players. Because we do have concern for our fallen leader. That’s exactly who he was; I don’t know any other way to say it.”

But the Lions are hopeful they can turn that concern for Campbell into an on-field honoring of everything he represents. Campbell is one of the hardest-working players on the team, and they know one of the best ways to honor him is to attack the week as he would.

“I think we owe it to him; we owe it to all of ourselves to make sure we’re locked in, and we make the most of this,” Campbell said. “And so, it’s balancing; you’re human and you know it, you want to acknowledge it. It’s a lot, but if that’s weighing that heavy and that’s where your mind’s at, it’s not going to be good going in this game, and that’s where you can get hurt as well.”

“We’re honoring him by the way that we prepare. We’re preparing like he prepares,” Montgomery added. “That’s what we’re talking with each other about. As players, as coaches, we’re going to prepare like he prepares. We’re going to play like he plays. We’re going to do the things that he would have us do. […] There’s no way around anybody in that locker room not feeling a certain way about him. But that same feeling that causes pain, it causes us to pursue the excellence of what Jack would want us to do in this situation, and that’s go prepare and get ready to go down and play a good football team and play to a high level this weekend.“

lions.headline: Detroit Lions’ Jack Campbell offers update: ‘I have full movement in my lower body’

Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell offered an update on Wednesday on his progress via an official statement from the team. Campbell has been hospitalized since taking a hit in Sunday’s game against the Minnesota Vikings that caused him to be carted away on a stretcher.

In the announcement, Campbell said that he has “full movement in my lower body,” while he is still “continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body.” Campbell expressed optimism and said he will take everything one day at a time.

Here’s the full statement from Campbell:

My family and I want to sincerely thank everyone for the overwhelming amount of love, prayers, and support we’ve received over the past few days. It means more to us than words can express.

I’m incredibly encouraged by the progress I’ve made in such a short period of time. I have full movement in my lower body, and I’m continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body. I know there’s still work ahead, but I remain very optimistic. I’m taking things one day at a time, staying positive, and focusing on getting better.

My faith in God has never been stronger. I know He has a plan for me, and I trust in that plan. I know there may be challenges ahead, but with my faith, my family, and so many people in my corner, I know we’ll get through this.

I especially want to thank the athletic trainers and medical personnel who responded and cared for me on the field. I know those were difficult moments, and I’m incredibly grateful for the professionalism, compassion, and care you showed me. The way you handled everything and looked after me when I needed it most is something I’ll never forget. From the bottom of my heart, thank you.

I also can’t say enough about the incredible care I’ve received from the medical team at Henry Ford Hospital and the Detroit Lions medical staff. They’ve been amazing to me and my family throughout this process, and I’m truly grateful for everything they’ve done.

To my teammates, coaches, and everyone in the Lions organization, I want you to know how much I love and appreciate you. This team is a family to me, and the way everyone has been there for me means everything. I’m proud to be a Detroit Lion and couldn’t ask to be surrounded by a better group of people.

One thing I’ve learned about Detroit is that this city is built on toughness, resilience, and grit. That’s exactly how I’m going to approach this challenge.

Please continue to keep me and my family in your prayers. We feel the love, and I can’t thank everyone enough.

God is good. My faith is strong.

Jack Campbell

lions.headline: 5 Lions vs. Dolphins thoughts after watching Miami’s loss to Patriots
lions.body:
Nov 1, 2026; Miami Gardens, Florida, USA; Miami Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis (2) drops back to throw a pass during the first quarter against the New England Patriots at Hard Rock Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Rich Storry-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect

To turn the page from Week 8 to Week 9, I spent some time early this week watching the Miami Dolphins’ most recent game to see what’s in store for the Detroit Lions.

Here are my five Lions vs. Dolphins thoughts after watching Miami’s 24-19 loss to the New England Patriots.

Note: It’s worth mentioning that it was a very rainy day in Miami, particularly at the start and end of the game.

Malik Willis holds onto the ball for a loooooong time

There could be a lot of reasons for it, but Willis holds onto the ball way too long in the pocket. Per NFL Pro, Willis’ 3.05 average seconds to throw is third-longest in the league. Is it taking Willis too long to go through his progressions, is he too hesitant to trust his eyes, or is his young receiving corps just not getting open? It’s hard to say from my vantage point, but it certainly is an opportunity for the Lions to get home against Willis.

Thus far, Willis has taken 21 sacks—the seventh most in the NFL—and the Dolphins have the second-highest sack rate in the NFL (10.3%).

The Patriots got to Willis five times in the first half, before backing down a little in the second.

This could be a big Tyleik Williams game

Miami had an extremely hard time stopping Patriots nose tackle Cory Durden in this game. He set career highs in pressure (three), quarterback hits (three), and sacks (1.5). Prior to this game, Durden had never recorded a sack and only had two quarterback hits since starting his NFL career, coincidentally in Detroit, in 2023.

Miami is particularly vulnerable on the right side of the line, where second-year right guard Jonah Savaiinaea is the 66th (out of 75) PFF-graded guard (47.9), and right tackle Austin Jackson is the lowest-graded tackle in football (44.6).

Williams is having a strong start to his second season, remaining a force in the run game (Dolphins rank 21st in EPA/rush, 24th in success rate) while growing as a pass rusher. Obviously, look out for Alim McNeill, too, who is currently only behind Broncos defensive tackle Zach Allen in PFF pressures from interior defenders (31).

The Lions’ run game should find success

Last week, the Lions found success pounding the rock right up the middle of the Vikings’ defense. That should be the game plan once again against the Dolphins. Rhamondre Stevenson toughed out 82 yards on 19 carries (4.3 YPC), as the Patriots produced a 45.2% success rate on the ground—ninth-highest of all Week 8 performances.

For the year, Miami ranks 21st in EPA/rush allowed and 30th in success rate (43.9%).

So they aren’t giving up a ton of explosive plays on the ground, but you can certainly grind them down. I would not be surprised to see another solid workload from Sione Vaki.

But Miami does have some dudes on defense

Miami’s defense as a whole won’t likely be up for the task against the Lions’ high-flying offense. The Dolphins rank 24th in points per game allowed (25.9) and 25th in yards per play allowed.

However, there are a couple of players who are playing well and capable of game-changing plays. The first is edge rusher Josh Uche. While Uche only has two sacks this year (one against the Patriots), he’s produced PFF’s ninth-highest run defense grade among edge defenders (76.0).

On the next level, rookie linebacker Jacob Rodriguez flashed against the Patriots. He had a teach-tape punchout and was second on the team with eight tackles. His rookie season has seen some ups and downs, but don’t be surprised if he makes a big play or two against the Lions.

The game wasn’t as close as the score

While the Dolphins only lost by five and they held a 10-point lead at halftime, this game did not feel like it was truly competitive between the teams.

For one, the Patriots made a ton of mistakes in the first half. They fumbled inside their own red zone, missed a 40-yard field goal, and had a ton of untimely penalties (seven in total). In the second half, the Patriots dropped an easy interception, and they had a game-clinching pick erased by an away-from-the-play offsides penalty.

And the Dolphins only made it close thanks to a prevent-defense touchdown with just over two minutes, because a Patriots defender fell down for an easy 35-yard touchdown.

On a per play basis, the Patriots produced more yards per play (5.3 vs. 4.5), and had a much higher success rate (49.1% vs. 43.8%). If you take away garbage-time stats, the difference is even bigger in success rate (52.9% vs. 39.3%).

Did we really get beat that bad? Comparing offensive success rates for NFL games in Week 8: pic.twitter.com/i4tQhlOtNa
— Sam Hoppen (@SamHoppen) November 2, 2026

If the Lions can avoid making self-inflicted mistakes, they should be able to win comfortably, despite the fact that Miami has kept each of their last four games within a touchdown.

lions.headline: Mailbag: Could the Detroit Lions target a linebacker at NFL trade deadline?
lions.body:
Oct 18, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Philadelphia Eagles linebacker Zack Baun (53) in action against the Carolina Panthers Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect

The NFL trade deadline is now less than a week away. If teams want to add talent via a trade, it must happen by 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday, November 10. After that, the only talent acquisition can come via free agency or waivers.

The Detroit Lions’ interest in a cornerback is no secret. The team openly admitted they were involved in talks for Joey Porter Jr., although the Dallas Cowboys apparently outbid them. Cornerback sure seems like it’s still on the table, but could Detroit’s strategy shift after losing several players to injury on Sunday against the Minnesota Vikings?

With rookie Jimmy Rolder out for the year and All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell out indefinitely with a neck injury, suddenly linebacker seems like a pretty serious need. This week, the Lions have backfilled their depth chart with special teams pieces in KJ Britt and (reportedly) Owen Pappoe. But can they trust players like Derrick Barnes, Malcolm Rodriguez, and Trevor Nowaske to hold starting roles? Or do they need to make an aggressive move to raise the ceiling of the room and fortify the middle of the field?

On this week’s Midweek Mailbag podcast, we discuss the Lions’ options at the NFL trade deadline, and outline a couple of names we’d like to see the Lions consider. At the top of that list is undoubtedly Eagles linebacker Zack Baun. The 29-year-old All-Pro linebacker is on a very manageable contract for Detroit (salaries of $1.215M, $1.345M, and $1.39M from 2026-28, plus a $14 million option bonus in 2027). It makes a little less sense for the Eagles (over $16M in dead cap), but if the Lions could make it worth it with draft compensation, they could get a deal done. And with the Eagles 2-6—losers of six straight—forced to play Tanner McKee at quarterback, it may make sense to acquire as much draft captial as possible.

Other linebacker options discussed: Buccaneers’ Alex Anzalone and Dolphins’ Jordyn Brooks.

We also talk about whether the Lions’ strategy should change considering how competitive the NFC North is this year. Does it make sense to get in an arms race with the Chicago Bears after their acquisition of Jeffrey Simmons? Or is that actually a reason to pull back this year and wait for a time in which things feel more open?

And we talk about a lot of topics beyond the trade deadline, including:

How the Lions’ “sidecar” formation was the perfect antidote to Brian Flores

Why didn’t Ennis Rakestraw play much vs. Minnesota?

What’s with the Lions’ short-yardage issues?

Is it actually better to have the 5th or 6th seed in the NFC rather than the No. 2 seed?

Should the Lions consider extending Christian Mahogany this offseason?

How many carries for Sione Vaki is the sweet spot?

Check out the show below, or find us on your favorite podcasting platform by searching “Pride of Detroit.”

As always, you can also catch the podcast on our YouTube page and Twitch channel. On this week’s show, we went through some more Movember shenanigans, including eating something called earthworm jerky. All available on the video portion only.

It appears the Detroit Lions will be adding even more linebacker depth to the team in the aftermath of serious injuries to Jack Campbell and Jimmy Rolder. In addition to reportedly signing KJ Britt from the Patriots’ practice squad, the Lions will also be signing linebacker Owen Pappoe (physical pending), according to a report from CBS Sports.

Pappoe, who visited the Lions on Tuesday per the transaction wire, was a third-round pick of the Arizona Cardinals in 2023. Over the next three years, Pappoe played in nearly every game for Arizona (49 total), mostly on special teams—945 snaps on teams, 341 on defense.

Pappoe was waived by the Cardinals as part of their roster cuts this year, but he was claimed by the Tennessee Titans the next day. He appeared in one game before the Titans released him a month ago.

Pappoe gives the Lions extra depth on special teams, and he also has an intriguing athletic profile.

It will be interesting to see how the Lions’ linebacker room shakes out with Rolder out of the year and Campbell out indefinitely. On Monday, Lions coach Dan Campbell seemed to express confidence in three linebackers who will likely become the team’s starters: Derrick Barnes, Malcolm Rodriguez, and Trevor Nowaske.

“Luckily we have some depth in there with Rodrigo and Nowaske and Barnes,” Campbell said. “Those three guys and Amen (Ogbongbemiga)’s been up for us, which is good. And then we have got (LB Joe) Bachie ready to roll.”

Britt will likely take up one of those spots, but the Lions will also have to create a spot on the practice squad for Pappoe. michigan.headline: 3 bold predictions for Michigan Football vs Michigan State
michigan.body:
ANN ARBOR, MI - OCTOBER 26: Michigan Wolverines defensive end Josaiah Stewart (0) and the team celebrate their 24-17 victory to keep the Paul Bunyan Trophy during the Michigan Wolverines versus the Michigan State Spartans game on Saturday October 26, 2024 at Michigan Stadium in Ann Arbor, MI. (Photo by Steven King/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images

This weekend, the Michigan Wolverines are trying to do something they haven’t done since Sept. 19: win back-to-back games. The Wolverines beat Western Michigan, Oklahoma and UTEP to open the season, but have gone loss, loss, win, loss, win since then. That trend needs to end this weekend against Michigan State.

While last week offered some encouragement in a few areas, it was a performance that left most fans disappointed. Rutgers is as bad as it gets in the Big Ten, and despite out-gaining the Scarlet Knights by nearly 200 yards, only allowing three completions, gaining 14 more first downs and nearly doubling up in time of possession, it was a one-score game that came down to the wire.

Like we’ve seen so many times this season, the Wolverines played down to their competition. They were fortunate to win, but in a rivalry game, that won’t fly. Let’s make some bold predictions for this weekend’s matchup against Michigan State.

Michigan will double Michigan State’s yardage

There’s no doubt about it, Michigan is more talented than Michigan State. Does that mean the Wolverines are going to win? No. Michigan is also more talented than Iowa and Minnesota, and we saw how those games went. Still, the talent advantage will play a factor.

Both teams struggle offensively, as the Wolverines (second-worst in the Big Ten) and Spartans (worst) have the two worst offenses in the Big Ten. However, Michigan has a massive advantage defensively. In total defense in all of college football, Michigan is ranked No. 3 out of 138 while Michigan State is No. 64. The Wolverines have a championship level defense and are going up against an offense that is depleted and struggling.

Based on that alone, the Wolverines shouldn’t have an issue winning the game if they play clean football and don’t beat themselves. I think Michigan will at least double up MSU in the yardage department.

Michigan will miss 3+ field goals

Speaking of beating themselves, one big issue that has added itself to the mix the last couple weeks has been the kicking game. If a 32-yard field goal is made against Indiana, Michigan probably wins that game, and without more missed kicks against Rutgers, that game is a lot less stressful down the stretch. Trey Butkowski has missed four field goals the last two weeks, and two of them were from 35 yards or closer.

The Wolverines have opened up the kicking competition this week, but even if it’s someone new, it’s a college kicker taking his first career kicks under the lights in front of 110,000+ people in a rivalry game. Either way, I don’t feel good, so I think the Wolverines kicking woes continue, resulting in three missed field goals.

Michigan State wins, 20-17

While I stated Michigan is more talented and should win by playing clean football, I haven’t seen anything this season that gives me a reason to believe that. At the end of the day, I’m looking at which coaching staff I trust more to get their team up for a rivalry game. I do not trust Kyle Whittingham in that regard right now. His comments from this week calling the game the Super Bowl “particularly for them” tells me he does not understand the importance. It is the Ohio State game? No, but this is still a massive rivalry game that should be treated as such.

Whittingham’s lack of emotion and lack of concern about the clear issues this team has are the things that worry me the most. I think he will get a big wake up call this weekend, because if the Wolverines continue to play sloppy football and let lesser opponents hang around, they will lose a game like this one. If you think people are unhappy with Whittingham and the program right now, just imagine what would happen in they lose this one.

Michigan has only had one game this season that wasn’t a one-score game (UTEP). Despite the talent advantage, all signs point to this being a tight battle, and the Wolverines aren’t going to keep getting away with letting their opponents hang around.

michigan.headline: Recruiting Roundup: Michigan to host 5-star CB for 2nd time this fall

Michigan cornerback Zeke Berry (10) intercepts a pass intended for Indiana wide receiver Nick Marsh (11) during the second half at Michigan Stadium in Ann Arbor on Saturday, Oct. 24, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co

Welcome to the Recruiting Roundup, our twice-per-week series breaking down the latest developments on the recruiting trail for the Michigan Wolverines. We’ll keep you up to date on the top targets, the visits they take, the predictions that analysts make, and everything in between. Here’s what you need to know today…

Five-star CB Nasir Richardson plans to return to Michigan

Michigan is set to get another visit from the top cornerback in the 2028 class. Nasir Richardson plans to return to Ann Arbor this weekend, according to Ethan McDowell of The Wolverine. The five-star out of Newark (N.J.) Malcolm X Shabazz is the No. 8 overall prospect and No. 1 cornerback in the class.

Richardson first visited Michigan for the Oklahoma game and hit it off with cornerbacks coach Jernaro Gilford. He was already thinking about a return trip by the time he got home, according to McDowell.

“The coaches, they was very welcoming,” Richardson told McDowell. “I know they’re supposed to do that, but I really felt it.”

His father, Dominique, came away impressed, too.

“It showed us real college football up close. The tradition, the fans, the facilities, it was high-level stuff,” Dominique told Steve Wiltfong of Rivals.

Richardson had Michigan and Penn State standing out before an October visit to Miami, and he now considers the Hurricanes a top option. With Miami gaining ground, Michigan gets another chance this weekend to build on the relationship Gilford started during the Oklahoma visit.

Four-star LB Skylar Alston sets Sunday commitment date

Skylar Alston will announce his commitment Sunday, Nov. 8. The 2028 linebacker from Raleigh (N.C.) Cardinal Gibbons is down to Michigan, South Carolina, Tennessee, Kentucky, North Carolina and UCLA. He’s the No. 171 overall prospect and No. 14 linebacker in the Rivals Industry Ranking.

“Now feels like the right time for me to commit,” Alston told Anna Adams of 247Sports. “I have been talking to my family and praying about it, and I’m ready to do it.”

Alston visited all six finalists this season. He’s been to North Carolina more times than he can count and has made several trips to Tennessee, but his one visit to Ann Arbor made an impression.

“I visited once and it blew me away, just everything they have to offer,” Alston said. “I love the linebacker play.”

Should he commit to the Wolverines, he would be the first member of their 2028 class following kicker Ryan Jung reclassifying to the 2027 class.

Stanford commit to take official visit to Michigan

Michigan offered Braden Chaffin last week, and the 2027 in-state offensive lineman will take an official visit this weekend, per Allen Trieu of Rivals. The 6-foot-6, 290-pound Sterling Heights Stevenson senior remains committed to Stanford, but Michigan will be the first other school he’s visited since pledging to the Cardinal.

Chaffin had already heard from Michigan about a game day visit and figured offensive line coach Jim Harding was calling to just follow up with him. Instead, Harding offered him a scholarship and told him he could see a role for him on Michigan’s offensive line.

“Every kid from Michigan dreams of playing for the Wolverines, so I personally feel like I couldn’t pass up this opportunity to see what the new staff and university are about,” Chaffin said.

Chaffin originally committed to Miami (Ohio) before flipping to Stanford after an official visit back in this summer. He told Trieu that two things have kept him committed to the Cardinal.

“The main thing that has kept me committed to Stanford was the relationships I have built with the coaches and the education,” Chaffin said.

We’ll see if Michigan can make up some ground this weekend.

michigan.headline: Michigan Football’s Blake Frazier reveals how he learned he was being moved from LT to RT
michigan.body:
Michigan offensive lineman Blake Frazier (77) celebrates 17-10 win over Oklahoma at Michigan Stadium in Ann Arbor on Saturday, Sept. 12, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co

Michigan offensive lineman Blake Frazier spent the spring, fall camp, and even some of last season at left tackle. But then right tackle Andrew Sprague went down with an injury early this season, and Frazier had to flip sides almost overnight.

On In The Trenches with Jon Jansen, Frazier explained how he has handled the adjustment and what it has taught him about the offensive line’s struggles in the run game.

Frazier found out he was going to be playing right tackle the day before the UTEP game. He had gone to offensive line coach Jim Harding’s office with a question about the game plan, and Harding gave him an unexpected look.

“He was like, ‘Can I tell you something without you freaking out?’” Frazier said. “I was like, ‘What’s going on?’ He goes, ‘You’re probably playing right tackle tomorrow.’”

Frazier had spent the whole week preparing for the game from the left side, only to be told he’ll be playing a different position.

“It’s definitely not what you expect to hear after practicing on one side all week and going through a game plan on one side,” Frazier said. “But it’s something they needed me to do, and so I was happy to do it.”

The most difficult adjustment for Frazier, he revealed to Jansen, was pass protection.

“The run game is the run game — you’re trying to put people on the ground,” Frazier said. “But with pass protection, you train your left leg and your right leg to do one thing. You’ve got a post foot and your slide foot, and now you’ve got to flip it. My pass set just didn’t feel as consistent. It was a lot more uncomfortable.”

Frazier said that has aspect of playing on the right side of the line has improved with reps. He estimated he has now played about five games on the right side, and it is becoming more comfortable.

The move also changed who Frazier is playing immediately next to. On the left side, he and guard Evan Link had to build their chemistry from scratch, since Link was a tackle last season. On the right side, he lines up next to Brady Norton, who already had his footwork and technique established at guard.

“My big thing was getting as comfortable as I could as quickly as possible, but also not stepping on his toes in any way,” Frazier said. “I didn’t want to make (Norton) uncomfortable with anything I was doing. Just getting reps over and over and over again was the best way to get comfortable quick.”

Michigan’s ground game has struggled for much of the 2026 season, and Frazier was candid about why that may be the case.

“Movement has been the biggest one that we’ve been struggling with,” Frazier said. “Sometimes you’ve got to wait for the defense to declare before you can get locked on. Our big thing has been patience, square shoulders and short steps. You can never have too short of steps. Your shoulders can never be too square. You can never be low enough.”

Frazier pointed to the Rutgers game as a step forward. Michigan ran for 161 yards on Saturday against the Scarlet Knights, and Frazier said downhill runs were the key.

“Getting guys covered up and fitting onto blocks was the big emphasis, and letting our backs find the hole and go from there,” Frazier said. “It wasn’t the most explosive run game. … It’s a step in the right direction. Coach Harding was saying in film this morning that we feel like we’re really close.”

With Michigan State up next, Frazier made his rivalry stance clear. Last year’s win in East Lansing was his first career start.

“It’s in-state bragging rights. It’s about establishing who runs the state,” Frazier said. “My personal goal is to never lose to Michigan State while I’m here.

“Focus on your one-eleventh. At the end of the day, this is going to be the dirtiest game that you ever play in, and it’s going to be a dogfight.”

Frazier has taken on more of a leadership role this season, and he acknowledged how hard that is when the results have not matched expectations.

“That’s been the tricky part for sure, how do you motivate guys to keep going when the results aren’t exactly what you want them to be?” Frazier said. “My personal motivation has been, what would my dad do to get to play another game? I owe it to everybody that’s ever put on the winged helmet to give it my all, regardless of what’s been going on with the team and the results.”

Frazier has had a lot asked of him this season. He moved sides on short notice, took on a bigger leadership role, and kept putting his head down and going to work despite how everything has gone this year. If the offensive line is as close to turning the corner as Harding believes, the Michigan State game is certainly a chance to show it.

michigan.headline: ‘He’s a natural playmaker’: Michigan Football is confident in QB Tommy Carr’s development
michigan.body:
Tommy Carr of the Michigan Wolverines lines up prior to the snap during an NCAA football game at SHI Stadium in Piscataway, United States, on October 31, 2026. (Photo by Dan Squicciarini/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images

Michigan quarterback Tommy Carr has a long way to go in his development and growth as the program’s starting signal caller. However, the freshman has displayed more than enough potential to have confidence in his future.

Carr was spectacular in every sense in a 28-21 win over Rutgers last week, totaling a season-high 320 yards and three touchdowns, completing 22-of-27 attempts. It was a great performance for a freshman’s first road start.

“He played a complete game,” head coach Kyle Whittingham said. “His ability to rip off key runs, do a good job with his reads, progression and decision-making. I can’t say enough good things about how he played. It was a very good game.”

"I liked everything about what he did."

🗣️ Kyle Whittingham on Tommy Carr's Week 9 performance at Rutgers pic.twitter.com/oqaPPeoXCK
— Big Ten Football (@B1Gfootball) November 2, 2026

Not only did he showcase impressive accuracy and decision-making in the passing game, but Carr’s ability to escape the pocket and make clutch plays on the ground proved to be one of the biggest factors in Michigan coming out with a win.

“He’s a natural playmaker,” tight end Hogan Hansen told the media. “He just has a knack for spreading the ball around. He’s not going to stare down his first read. He’s aware of how the play develops and he’s always keeping his eyes open.”

Carr’s composure and poise are always brought up by his coaches and teammates when asked about him, and that was evident in the win at Rutgers. He constantly came up with clutch plays in his second career start.

“The main word I use for Tommy is ‘poise,’” offensive lineman Evan Link said on Tuesday. “He’s very calm in the huddle and pocket. That kind of radiates to our offense. He’s in control and he’s very calm. I think those are great qualities for a quarterback.”

With the pass rush barreling down on him and the game still in the balance, he didn’t blink. Carr remained posied, escaping the pocket and alluding multiple defenders on his way to scoring the game-winning touchdown.

Tommy Carr scrambles across the goal line to put @UMichFootball in front 🙌

Watch on BTN pic.twitter.com/aVpJN4N5xT
— Big Ten Network (@BigTenNetwork) October 31, 2026

“The moment hasn’t been too big for him,” quarterbacks coach Koy Detmer Jr. told the media on Wednesday. “He’s just calm, cool and collected. He has that look in his eye and he has been able to really handle everything that we have been doing up to this point.

“There are some guys that can feel the pressure and some guys that can’t, and Tommy just has that feel. He has a very good knack for it. Tommy has a really nice understanding of when he has time and when there’s pressure.”

Carr was thrust into action as Michigan trailed Penn State at halftime a few weeks back, and he led a comeback win and scored the game-winning touchdown. Just two weeks later, he continued to showcase his potential in the win at Rutgers.

“I’m super proud of him. It’s been fun to watch him from the second half against Penn State until now,” Detmer said. “We felt confident that when the moment was presented to him, he would be ready to step in and help us win games.”

Even though it hasn’t been perfect, Carr’s overall body of work since taking over the starting job has been promising. It will be key for the freshman quarterback to continue improving, and the program is confident in him getting better and leading the way.

michigan.headline: Positive statement from Jack Campbell
michigan.body:
Positive statement from Jack Campbell

I've been terrified of this situation all week as days passed with no news. Here's Jack's statement:
"My family and I want to sincerely thank everyone for the overwhelming amount of love, prayers, and support we've received over the past few days. It means more to us than words can express.
I'm incredibly encouraged by the progress I've made in such a short period of time. I have full movement in my lower body, and I'm continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body. I know there's still work ahead, but I remain very optimistic. I'm taking things one day at a time, staying positive, and focusing on getting better.
My faith in God has never been stronger. I know He has a plan for me, and I trust in that plan. I know there may be challenges ahead, but with my faith, my family, and so many people in my corner, I know we'll get through this.
I especially want to thank the athletic trainers and medical personnel who responded and cared for me on the field. I know those were difficult moments, and I'm incredibly grateful for the professionalism, compassion, and care you showed me. The way you handled everything and looked after me when I needed it most is something I'll never forget. From the bottom of my heart, thank you.
I also can't say enough about the incredible care I've received from the medical team at Henry Ford Hospital and the Detroit Lions medical staff. They've been amazing to me and my family throughout this process, and I'm truly grateful for everything they've done.
To my teammates, coaches, and everyone in the Lions organization, I want you to know how much I love and appreciate you. This team is a family to me, and the way everyone has been there for me means everything. I'm proud to be a Detroit Lion and couldn't ask to be surrounded by a better group of people.
One thing I've learned about Detroit is that this city is built on toughness, resilience, and grit. That's exactly how I'm going to approach this challenge.
Please continue to keep me and my family in your prayers. We feel the love, and I can't thank everyone enough.
God is good. My faith is strong."
Jack Campbell
